finding: The legacy retry path added a completed wait interval again on every retry, erasing consumed working time and allowing a genuinely over-budget assignment.

repair.identity: Each wait is keyed by the wait operation id (persisted on the step as wait_operation_id) and recorded once in budget.wait_credits.
repair.boundaries: start = active_wait.started_at / persisted waiting.since / wait operation claimed_at; end = the recorded external response at (or the actual resume time). Never a later retry timestamp or an unrelated step timestamp.
repair.legacy: A legacy assignment with paused_seconds > 0 records the interval as already credited and adds zero. A legacy assignment with paused_seconds == 0 credits the actual interval once.
repair.cas: Wait entry, response resolution, resume and retry all run inside the existing assignment mutate/CAS; the wait_credits ledger makes the credit idempotent under concurrent/restarted retries.
repair.attempts: A pre-dispatch budget refusal keeps its actual attempt count and uses pre_dispatch_budget_refusal so the gate admits the repair retry; a real adapter failure still consumes an attempt.
